2027-03-20.title: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Lent
readings: I will make them one nation in the land
The Lord will guard us as a shepherd guards his flock
Jesus was about to die to gather into one the dispersed children of God
2027-03-20.alt: Lenten weekday of the fifth week. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. From the Fifth Sunday of Lent crosses and images may be veiled until the Passion is celebrated (where the bishops' conference allows). Liturgical colour: violet. Tomorrow Holy Week begins with Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord; parishes may announce the time and place of the blessing of palms and the procession.
2027-03-20.verse: He did not say this on his own, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God.
theo: On the eve of Holy Week the Church reads a promise of unity. Ezekiel had seen the kingdom of David split into two, Israel and Judah, and then both scattered in exile. Now God promises: “I will take the people of Israel from the nations… I will make them one nation in the land… and one king shall be king over them all. Never again shall they be two nations.” He will cleanse them from their idols, give them “one shepherd,” his servant David, and make “a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant… My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” Instead of a Psalm, we sing Jeremiah's song of the shepherd who gathers: “He who scattered Israel will gather him, and will keep him as a shepherd a flock… I will turn their mourning into joy.”

The Gospel shows how this gathering will happen. Jesus has just raised Lazarus at Bethany. Many believe in him; others report to the authorities. The council meets in fear: if we let him go on, “the Romans will come and destroy both our holy place and our nation.” Caiaphas, the high priest that year, gives a cold political calculation: “it is better for you to have one man die for the people than to have the whole nation destroyed.” John sees a hidden prophecy in it: Jesus was indeed about to die for the nation, “and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God.” What Caiaphas meant as expediency, God turned into salvation. We must read this carefully: the decision belongs to a small group of leaders in a frightened hour, and the Church teaches that the Passion cannot be charged against all the Jews then living, nor against the Jews of today (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 597). In truth, Christ died for the sins of all of us. The chapter ends with pilgrims in the Temple asking each other, “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the festival, will he?” Tomorrow we have the answer: he comes, riding on a colt, to lay down his life and gather us into one.
outline: Ask: what divides your family, parish or village, and who can bring it back together?

Caiaphas speaks more than he knows.

live: Take one step today to heal a division in your family or among friends: a call, a visit, a word of peace.
Plan your week now: the Palm Sunday procession, confession, the Chrism Mass if possible, and the Triduum.
2027-03-20.prayer: Good Shepherd, you laid down your life to gather into one the scattered children of God. Heal the divisions in our families, our parishes and among Christians. As Holy Week begins, let us go up with you to Jerusalem, to your cross and to your resurrection. Amen.
altar: The Eucharist is the sacrament of unity: one bread, one body. Around the altar Christ gathers into one the dispersed children of God, as he promised by his death.

quick: Ezekiel promises that God will make his scattered people one nation with one shepherd.
Caiaphas unknowingly prophesied that Jesus would die to gather God's children into one.
Holy Week begins tomorrow: Jesus comes to the feast to give his life.
2027-03-20.action: Make peace with one person today before Holy Week begins.
2027-03-20.question: Am I a person who gathers people together, or one who scatters?

family.explain: After Jesus raised Lazarus, some leaders were afraid and decided that Jesus must die. The high priest said: it is better for one man to die for the people. Without knowing it, he was saying something true: Jesus would die to bring all God's children together into one family.
family.intention: We pray for families that are divided, and for unity among all Christians.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we are not talking to? How can we make peace before Palm Sunday?”

illus: Two brothers in Ernakulam had not spoken for six years after a quarrel over a small piece of land. Their old mother asked only one thing for her birthday, which fell in Holy Week: that both sons would carry palms together in the procession. They came, stiff and silent, and walked side by side. By the time the Passion was read, the younger had put his hand on the older's shoulder. The land is still divided, their mother says, but my sons are not.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you died to gather into one the scattered children of God. Gather us into your one flock. Amen.
share: I will make them one nation… never again shall they be divided (Ezekiel 37:22). Where is there division around me?
It is better for you to have one man die for the people (John 11:50). What does it mean to me that Jesus died for me?
Surely he will not come to the festival, will he? (John 11:56). How will I welcome Jesus this Holy Week?
pm.resp: The Lord will guard us as a shepherd guards his flock.
interc: For Christian unity, that all who believe in Christ may be one.
For divided families, that they may be reconciled this Holy Week.
For the Holy Land and all places torn by conflict, that God may give a covenant of peace.
For the elect who will be baptized at the Easter Vigil.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus closely through Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to gather your scattered children. Make us one in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Ezekiel saw God's people broken into two kingdoms and scattered among the nations. And God promised: I will make them one nation… never again shall they be two nations… they shall all have one shepherd (Ezekiel 37:22, 24). God's dream is not a scattered people but one family.

In the Gospel, after Lazarus is raised, some leaders are afraid. Caiaphas says: it is better for you to have one man die for the people than to have the whole nation destroyed (John 11:50). He was thinking of politics. But John tells us he was prophesying: Jesus would die not only for the nation, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God (John 11:52).

We must hear this rightly. The Church teaches that the death of Jesus cannot be blamed on all the Jews of that time or on the Jewish people today. The deepest truth is that Jesus died for the sins of all of us, and freely gave his life. And what men intended for evil, God used for the salvation of the world.

The pilgrims in the Temple asked: will he come to the festival? Tomorrow is Palm Sunday. He comes. Let us go out to meet him with palms, and let us make peace with one another, so that he may gather us into one at his cross. Amen.
kids: Children, God wants all his children to be one big family. Jesus gave his life to bring everyone together. Tomorrow is Palm Sunday, and we will wave palms for Jesus our King! Today, if you have quarrelled with someone, go and make peace.

intro: Theme: “To gather into one the dispersed children of God.”
Ezekiel's promise, Caiaphas' unwitting prophecy, and the threshold of Holy Week.

q: My servant David shall be king over them; and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall follow my ordinances and be careful to observe my statutes.
I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also, and they will listen to my voice. So there will be one flock, one shepherd.
points.apply: Pray this week for Christian unity, and greet a Christian of another Church with warmth.

sub: A prophecy of salvation, and the death Christ freely accepted for all.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.

He did not say this on his own, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God.
points.apply: Say each day of Holy Week: Jesus, you died for me; gather me into your one family.

points.h: Will he come to the festival?
sub: He comes, to give his life.
q: Rejoice greatly, O daughter Zion! Shout aloud, O daughter Jerusalem! Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
They were looking for Jesus and were asking one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the festival, will he?”
points.apply: Come to the Palm Sunday procession tomorrow, and keep the whole of Holy Week with Jesus.

concl: God's will is to gather his scattered children into one.
Jesus comes to Jerusalem freely, to die for all and to make us one.
2027-03-20.resolve: Make peace with one person before Palm Sunday.
